articles.title: An HVAC technician explains why leaving the air conditioning on at night can be the smarter option
articles.excerpt: The real issue, he says, is how much heat builds up in the home before the unit ever switches on.
articles.author: anabel-blazquez
articles.imageCaption: An air conditioning unit mounted on an interior wall | EP
content: An HVAC technician says the real issue with nighttime cooling is not the running cost of the unit itself, but how much heat has already built up in the home before it switches on.
Running a unit at a moderate, steady setting overnight, he explains, is often more efficient than letting the home heat up and then cooling it aggressively in short bursts.
The advice comes as several regions continue to see unusually high overnight temperatures well into late summer.

articles.title: A simple, consistent routine is the real secret to staying fit later in life, trainers say
articles.excerpt: "Consistency is your best friend" is the advice trainers repeat most often to older clients.
articles.author: anabel-blazquez
articles.imageCaption: A group stretching session in a park | EP
content: Trainers say a simple, consistent routine matters more than intensity for clients looking to stay fit later in life.
"Consistency is your best friend" is the advice repeated most often, alongside a reminder that recovery time matters as much as the workouts themselves.
Several trainers also pointed to strength training, rather than cardio alone, as the most underused tool among older clients.

articles.title: Sleep specialists share what actually helps during a heatwave, and what doesn't
articles.excerpt: Cooling the room before bed matters more than any gadget, several specialists agree.
articles.author: anabel-blazquez
articles.imageCaption: A bedroom with blinds drawn against afternoon heat | EP
content: Sleep specialists say the most effective heatwave strategy is a simple one: cooling the bedroom well before bedtime rather than relying on gadgets once already in bed.
Closing blinds during the hottest hours of the day, they note, does more to keep a room cool overnight than any fan or cooling pillow used afterward.
Several specialists also cautioned against late, heavy meals during hot spells, saying digestion adds to the body's overnight heat load.

articles.title: Community walking groups are drawing record numbers, and organisers credit more than fitness
articles.excerpt: Participants say the regular social contact matters as much as the exercise itself.
articles.author: anabel-blazquez
articles.imageCaption: A group walking together along a park path | EP
content: Community walking groups are reporting record participation this year, with organisers crediting the format's social element as much as its fitness benefits.
Many participants say the regular, low-pressure social contact has been the bigger draw, particularly among those who live alone or recently retired.
Public health officials have taken notice, with several municipalities now funding walking groups as part of broader wellbeing initiatives.
